stem:
Kavya scores $16$ marks out of $20$ on one test and $21$ marks out of $25$ on another.

Which two claims about comparing her percentages are correct?

options.text: $21$ is larger than $16$, so the second score is the higher percent.
Convert both to percentages first ($80\%$ and $84\%$), because the wholes $20$ and $25$ differ.
A larger raw score need not be a larger percent when the totals differ.
Compare the raw scores on a third unrelated whole of $100$ marks she did not take.

teacher.key_rationale: Different wholes require percentage (or common-base) comparison; raw marks alone are not enough. Ranking by raw marks, or inventing a third whole, breaks the hinge.
